feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital/public-sector communications roles: the positioning is clear, experience progression is logical, and the scope feels substantive. Writing is polished overall, but impact would improve with sharper outcomes, less duplication across skills sections, and a few consistency edits.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative: strong headline, relevant summary, and visible progression from coordinator to director to consultant.  
- Good credibility signals: named employer, large-scale website migration, analytics stack, team/platform ownership, and concrete project examples.  
- Writing is generally concise and professional, with solid domain vocabulary and mission-driven alignment.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable outcomes beyond activity/scope: e.g., % growth, engagement lifts, efficiency gains, adoption rates, cost savings, or campaign results. Several bullets describe responsibilities more than impact.  
- Reduce redundancy: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would tighten structure and free space for achievements.  
- Fix stylistic/grammar consistency: “social, and multimedia” should be “social and multimedia”; maintain consistent punctuation in bullets; “A2/Learning” reads awkwardly—use “A2 (learning)”; “10×20-foot” may be clearer as “10 x 20-foot.” No major misspellings detected.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear seniority and domain focus. It reads well, but it’s slightly broad and repeats themes covered in Core Competencies and Work Experience; adding one concrete scale signal would make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten phrasing and reduce list-like structure; replace “building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind” with more direct language.
- Add a concrete scale/relevance cue from recent experience, e.g., “10,000+ page Drupal migration” or “3.5M annual page views,” if you want stronger impact.
- Consider sharpening “AI-enabled user experiences” to “AI-enabled search and content experiences” for specificity and alignment with recent projects.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing web platforms, governance, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise website transformation, analytics and reporting infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production, and AI-enabled search and content experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Analytics infrastructure,” “editorial systems,” and “AI-enabled…” closely mirror Core Competencies; keep the intro higher-level if those sections remain.
- “Public-sector communications” and “mission-driven organizations” are slightly overlapping; one may be enough.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block largely repeats the header and Topline Skills. It would be sharper if it emphasized distinctive, senior-level strengths and used tighter, more parallel phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use more concise, leadership-oriented wording and keep all items structurally parallel.
- Replace broader phrases like “multi-channel communications operations” with more specific, higher-value terms tied to scope and systems.
- Consider this rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, dashboarding and reporting systems • Cross-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integrations • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia, studio and livestream production
- If space allows elsewhere, prioritize the most recent/high-impact capabilities: AI-enabled search, enterprise Drupal modernization, analytics infrastructure, and governance.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section overlaps heavily with the header summary and all three Topline Skills blocks.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” is already well established in the header and work experience.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it largely repeats achievements already covered in recent roles. Tightening the language and adding clearer outcomes or scope would make it feel more distinctive and impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add dates or “Selected Recent Projects” framing to reinforce recency and separate this from core experience.
- Use parallel, tighter phrasing: “Built,” “Led,” “Developed,” “Launched,” and trim filler like “designed for continued campaign growth.”
- Add 1 concrete detail per project where possible: audience, scale, platform, or business purpose.
- Standardize style and punctuation; spell out “10 x 20-foot” consistently and consider “AI-powered” instead of “AI-enabled” for cleaner wording.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series closely overlap with the current freelance role and NACo experience.
- Video/studio and campaign storytelling themes also echo Work Experience and Topline Skills, so this section should emphasize standout examples, not restate responsibilities.

items.title: Coleman Davis

Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Website

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear relevance, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with the header, competencies, and NACo entries. Tighten it around distinctive consulting impact, named initiatives, and outcomes.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + client value: “Embedded full-time consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital strategy, Drupal campaign delivery, content operations, and enterprise web improvements.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 3–4 sharper ones; e.g. combine systems/workflows/analytics/governance into one operational leadership bullet.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages supported, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, search accuracy gains, publishing speed improvements, stakeholder teams served.
- Rephrase for impact: “Led AI-enabled search initiative, defining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, and discovery UX” and “Built modular Drupal microsites and member toolkits for advocacy and storytelling campaigns.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, workflows, analytics, and enterprise web improvement” repeats language already used in the summary and NACo Director role.
- Detailed project examples may duplicate the “Recent Projects” section; keep this entry focused on role-level ownership and results.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale signals. It will be stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest transformation outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management points covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Replace the broad lead sentence with a sharper scope/outcome summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Reorder bullets to emphasize biggest wins first: website migration, analytics stack expansion, in-house studio build, then governance/operations.
- Make channel leadership more outcome-based: add email list size, engagement growth, social growth, production volume, or cost/time savings if available.
- Tighten phrasing for concision, e.g. “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal site serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ publishers.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this version focused on scale, strategy, and measurable performance.
- Video/studio language may overlap with footer projects; emphasize building organizational capability rather than recurring content production.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more clearly about executional leadership, channel growth, and cross-team coordination during this period.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and level: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, supporting advocacy messaging and organization-wide editorial coordination.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active and distinct from later studio work: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Sharpen operational impact: “Built stronger editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving coordination and content consistency.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Helped improve…” is weak and overlaps with the Director entry’s governance/workflow language; use a direct action verb.
- Avoid repeating broad channel oversight already covered in the Director role; focus this item on execution and process-building.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. Make it sharper, more senior, and more clearly tied to recent enterprise/public-sector leadership.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with tighter, less repetitive phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy for public-sector organizations
- Editorial governance and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Advocacy and stakeholder messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “Audience-focused content planning” for “Content governance and planning” if you want to emphasize systems leadership over editorial execution.
- If space allows elsewhere, add proof of scale instead of broad labels, e.g., “10,000+ page web ecosystems” or “50+ publisher environments.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” repeat the header/Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” also overlaps with Core Competencies; keep only one version across sections.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and recent strengths rather than repeat every technology.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Drop lower-priority or older items here, especially “jQuery,” unless it is required for target roles.
- Consider replacing “WordPress - SharePoint - Power Pages” with “Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint and Power Pages” to reduce list fatigue.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented: “CMS modernization and migration for high-volume public-sector sites”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section duplicates the “Technical + IT” section almost line-for-line; keep Topline Skills broader and reserve full tool inventory for Technical + IT.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” already appears in Core Competencies and the header summary.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it currently reads like a duplicate of the “Data, Analytics & Optimization” technical section and misses the strategic value you delivered in recent roles. Make this more outcome-oriented and leadership-level.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability statement: “Analytics strategy, reporting infrastructure & performance optimization”
- Tighten and elevate the bullets to: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio & Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework design • Executive/leadership reporting • SEO, UX and content performance analysis”
- If space allows, add one higher-level phrase tied to recent work: “Measurement strategy for enterprise web and campaign platforms”
- Keep only the most decision-making-oriented terms here; leave purely technical/platform detail to the Technical + IT section

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially overlaps with “Core Competencies: Analytics and reporting infrastructure” and “Technical + IT: Data, Analytics & Optimization”
- Avoid repeating the exact same tool list across sections; this section should emphasize strategic application, not inventory

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it’s generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Make it more senior and outcomes-oriented so it supports recent leadership roles rather than reading like a tool list.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to emphasize leadership scope: “Multimedia Production, Studio & Event Operations.”
- Tighten and elevate phrasing: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ and multi-camera studio systems • Studio buildout and operations • Virtual event production”
- If space allows, add scale/context instead of generic terms, e.g. “in-house studio operations” or “recurring advocacy video programming.”
- Consider replacing “video production and editing” with “video strategy, production and post-production” to better reflect director-level ownership.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” and “Hybrid and virtual event production” partially duplicate “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies.
- Tool-specific detail like PTZ/studio workflows also overlaps with “Multimedia & Creative Tools” in Technical + IT.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” section. This item should either be tightened to emphasize current/relevant platforms or expanded with light context that supports recent Drupal-led work.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize most relevant/current tools first: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages” is fine, but consider “Drupal (enterprise, Drupal 10) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- If space allows, add level/scope instead of just names: “Drupal (enterprise migrations, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- Keep phrasing parallel and concise; avoid mixing platforms with broader capabilities here.
- If this section is meant to be purely technical inventory, consider dropping the title repetition and renaming to “CMS Platforms.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely repeats “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills; consider merging or using one section for platform names and the other for capabilities.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent roles/projects, so avoid overexplaining it here.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools that support recent Drupal, AI search, and workflow work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as execution-focused tools, not broad coding languages alone: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Group by function for clarity: “Integrations & tagging: API integrations, Google Tag Manager”
- Keep newer, higher-signal tools prominent: “Edge/serverless & deployment: Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- If true, add specificity tied to recent work: “custom Drupal theming/components,” “search/API prototyping,” or “deployment automation”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” already appears in Topline Skills; consider shortening one version or removing overlap.
- “API integrations” and workflow tooling also echo Core Competencies; this section should stay tool-specific, not capability-based.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too broad and reads as an undifferentiated software list. It would be stronger if grouped by function and weighted toward tools that support your recent workflow automation/systems leadership.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to emphasize systems use, not just apps: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira/Asana • Slack/Teams”
- Group by category for clarity and concision: “Workflow automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project management: Jira, Asana | Collaboration: Slack, Teams”
- Drop lower-value/general tools unless they are core to current work; Basecamp and Trello feel older/lighter relative to recent enterprise work.
- If space allows, add a brief qualifier tied to impact: “used to streamline editorial planning, cross-team coordination, and platform operations”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies/Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim.
- Slack and Teams are generic collaboration tools; keep only if this section needs breadth rather than depth.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools for this profile, but the item is too bare and misses the strategic email/engagement context shown in recent NACo work. It should signal enterprise email operations rather than read like a generic software list.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms
- Reorder by likely depth/relevance: Higher Logic • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add scope in concise parentheticals: Higher Logic (newsletter/member communications) • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (journey automation/segmentation) • Mailchimp (campaign delivery)
- If space allows, strengthen with function over brand names: Email campaign operations • audience segmentation • automated journeys • newsletter publishing

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating “multi-channel communications” or newsletter scale here; that impact is already covered well in recent work experience.
- Don’t add analytics terms like A/B testing or reporting in this item; those already appear under Data, Analytics & Optimization.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” In the Technical + IT section, make it more tool-specific and drop broad capability terms that are already demonstrated in recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • Google Search Console
- Remove “Dashboarding” and “A/B testing” unless you can name the platform or method (e.g., Optimizely, VWO, GA4 experiments)
- Replace broad “SEO” with a tool/process term if applicable: Google Search Console, technical SEO, on-page SEO, or site search analysis
- If space allows, order by strongest/recent tools first: GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This nearly duplicates “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization”; consider keeping detail in one place only
- Recent NACo experience already proves analytics infrastructure leadership, so this line should stay as a concise tool stack, not repeat outcomes

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful “first in-house digital team” context, but the item is still broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and emphasize foundational contributions rather than leadership already covered later.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to stress early-stage build work: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Replace vague phrases like “high-impact digital content” with concrete outputs: website refresh support, livestream production, weekly video series production, channel publishing cadence.
- Add scale if available: number of livestreams/events, frequency of video updates, audience growth, email/social volume, or workflow improvements.
- Tighten the ending to show scope without overstating management: “provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate” or “helped onboard/support a junior team member.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the later “weekly advocacy video update”; differentiate this as the earlier launch/build phase.
- Avoid repeating workflow/governance language already used more strongly in the 2018–2024 roles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads broadly and undersells the most distinctive achievement. Since later NACo roles already cover digital leadership, this item should emphasize foundational innovation/research support plus the first-podcast launch.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the standout outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; launched the organization’s first podcast from concept through scripting and production.”
- Tighten generic phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” into clearer ownership: “Produced digital and multimedia content supporting program and policy communications.”
- If possible, add scope or result: number of projects supported, podcast episodes launched, internal stakeholders served, or audience/reach.
- Consider a two-part structure: one clause for research/program coordination, one for podcast/multimedia execution.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating broad “digital content/multimedia” language already covered in later NACo roles.
- Don’t overstate leadership in digital operations here; later roles show that progression more credibly.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills list, but it reads more like a mixed capability summary than a clean tools line. It also overlaps with stronger, more recent experience bullets and Topline Skills around multimedia production and studio operations.

Suggested edit:
- Tighten to software/tools only, and move workflow-based items elsewhere if you want to keep this section strictly technical.
- Rewrite as: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Podcast editing/production
- If livestream capability is important, make it more tool-specific: Livestream production tools / studio systems instead of “Livestream studio workflows.”
- Consider adding only tools you actively used in recent roles; if applicable, name platforms/hardware/software used for broadcast or streaming.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestream studio workflows” and “Podcast production” duplicate broader claims already covered in Core Competencies, Topline Skills, and NACo experience bullets.
- Since recent roles already establish multimedia leadership, this item should emphasize concrete tools rather than repeat functional areas.
